They should use a `None` default with a fresh list per call, and `build_report` should pass `result` through, so each call returns only its own titles.

```
KEEP  no callers outside report.py, no pre-existing tests — I own the contract here

```

content.text:
Fixed and verified.

## Cause

`add_section(title, sections=[])` — the default `[]` is evaluated **once, at function-definition time**, not per call. Every call that omitted `sections` appended into that same list object, so it grew for the life of the process.

The second half mattered too: `build_report` did `result = add_section(title)` without passing `result` in. It built a fresh `result = []` and then threw it away, depending entirely on the shared default to accumulate. So `sections=None` alone would have turned the bug into a different one — `build_report` returning only the last title.

## Change

```python
def add_section(title, sections=None):
    if sections is None:
        sections = []
    ...

def build_report(titles):
    result = []
    for title in titles:
        result = add_section(title, result)   # thread the accumulator
    return result
```

## What I ran

No test file existed, so I wrote `test_report.py` (4 cases) and ran it **before** the edit: 2 failed for precisely the expected reason — the leak crossed test-function boundaries, producing `['intro','body','summary','a']` where `['a']` was expected. After the edit all 4 pass, and a direct repro confirms three consecutive `build_report` calls in one process return `['intro','body']`, `['summary']`, `['summary']`.

Two notes on scope: `add_section` has no callers outside `report.py`, so no other code depended on the accumulating behaviour. And I kept its documented contract — a caller-supplied list is still appended to in place and returned, which the fourth test pins down.
